searchText: This is the 10M gas test test tweaked to 40M gas, hence `"pass":false` as the postHash won't line up. if this griefing vector is no longer relevant post-Shanghai, do we have an idea what the next-worst-case vector is post-shanghai so we can get an idea of worst case performance at higher gaslimits? https://mariusvanderwijden.github.io/blog/2024/01/11/GasLimit/ i agree with most of the underlying sentiment here, though I would quibble on some of the numbers presented and how they are presented. The important part that i'm not sure I agree with yet is that the existence of a DOS vector should prevent an increase in gas targets. i'm uncomfortable with the inductive nature of that. 🤔 Secondly, if I did accept it, it would put us in a world where our explanation to the public for a decision is necessarily opaque. I think this is an excellent discussion to have in a private forum as it likely includes undisclosed and not well-known issues. we're not talking about anything that hasn't been on reddit or a blog, but I'm happy to move elsewhere, not sure where that would be. I've removed the table now, sorry about that. Do you have a problem with the other numbers in the post? The idea of a dos vector preventing us from increasing gaslimits is very old, there has basically always been some dos (state, jumpdest, precompiles,...) in the past. Thus we could never talk about it as freely as we can today No, the other numbers/points in the post I have no qualm with, thank you. I understand the reasoning behind not wanting to push the gaslimit beyond X based on "secret knowledge", I think that is fine. My concern was with saying "we shouldn't go beyond 30M because in the past there were issues" which was the takeaway I was getting. I find that to be bad reasoning, however "among the known problems, none of them hurt at 40M" would to me be sound logic. Ah, yeah I understand! No I don't see a blocker (execution-wise) atm. But I'll do some more tests soon happy to connect via keybase/signal/telegram when you do "What if bug? Might destabilize other clients on same machine" isn't really a reason; as doesn't matter what the block size is, any bug could still do that; and other client is probably an L2 running at 75M gaslimit on L1's code base anyway but with cheaper fees, so if the big is going to be hit is still going to be hit
